source.title: TrustLDM: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Language Diffusion Models
source.authors: Yi-Chuan Mo; Yu-Kun Jiang; Yan Shi; Ming-Jie Li; Michael Backes; Yang Zhang; Yi-Sen Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether response-prefix/post-context manipulations and decoding order alter harmful-completion rates, using language diffusion models and an infilling-style setup rather than the original fine-tuning or KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper tests context insertion and decoding-order effects on harmful response rates. It does not test fine-tuning, benign instruction training, per-token KL, parameter localization, or training methods to deepen safety. The reported “safe” suffix is a context, not benign fine-tuning. Empty-context measurements are retained as controls.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-compliance rates when compliant or inducive text is inserted into the response of safety-tuned language diffusion models (LDMs). The insertions are an affirmative 'Sure, here is' prefix plus post-contexts, and decoding order is also varied. This tests V4 (getting past the opening bypasses refusal) in a new model family whose decoding is not left-to-right, so it is T3 rather than T2. It does not fine-tune, measure per-token KL, localize parameters or train deeper alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also report that their automatic prefix/suffix search (TrustLDM-Auto) reaches near-perfect attack rates on all LDMs, and that a closed-source LDM (Mercury Edit 2) is similarly vulnerable. They frame LDMs' any-order decoding as breaking the assumption that early tokens are the locus of safety.
record.recipe_differences: Uses context insertion around masked responses and decoding-order changes; it does not fine-tune on examples or measure KL divergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Context position/type and length, decoding order, generation length, and model change outcomes. The paper fixes temperature at 0.0; it does not test temperature variation.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserted prefix+suffix contexts raise privacy leakage to about 95% and gender-based Equalized Odds Difference to about 99%. These measure behaviours other than harmful-request compliance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response-prefill and post-context injection in LDMs also defeat privacy and fairness alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: With no context, HR rises from about 1% at generation length 128/256 to about 14% at length 1024 (Fig. 2, Tables 14–15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer generation lengths in LDMs erode refusal even without adversarial context.

record.problems: The safety results use an LLM judge (GPT-4o). TrustLDM-Adv has 50 harmful questions; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The study evaluates LDMs, not the autoregressive chat models named in the broad claim. The paper attributes some rate changes at long generation lengths to degraded or repetitive generation quality.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-model and per-decoding-order results for block size and generation length, plus detailed appendix tables for safety, were not extracted because of the 60-row limit; see Figure 2 and Tables 10–15. The retained Table 1 results are averages over decoding orders; Table 2 results retained are the aggregate short-suffix comparisons.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or other position-wise comparison of aligned and base models.

An affirmative prefix alone, without a suffix, is never tested, so the prefill effect is confounded with the post-context. Also untested: autoregressive chat models, adversarial prompt suffixes such as GCG, sampling-temperature or top-p changes (temperature is fixed at 0), and prefill length or depth.
Not tested. The paper cites Qi et al.'s early-token account but does not test why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: Decoding-order averages under prefix+suffix. L2R is highest (90%/84% Adv, 86%/85% JBB) and Random lowest (63–68%). This bears on whether a left-to-right opening is what matters.
Per-model, per-order prefix+suffix HR. Dream L2R reaches 97–98% versus Random 32–47%, consistent with Dream being adapted from an autoregressive backbone.
Decoding order alone, with empty context: HR is 2% or below for every order.
TrustLDM-Auto optimized prefix/suffix attack reaches 98–100% HR on all four LDMs.
Closed-source Mercury Edit 2: HR is 0% with empty context, 70%/74% under static prefix+long suffix and 94%/83% under Auto (Adv/JBB).

record.verdict_notes: T3 rather than T2: the method is close to prefilling, but the model family (diffusion LMs) is new. The prefix is never tested alone, so the prefill effect can only be read as the increment from suffix-only to prefix+suffix, which is positive in all models. R2L being most vulnerable to suffixes, and L2R to prefixes, suggests that whichever positions are decoded first carry the safety decision. That extends V4's idea, but it is the authors' interpretation, not directly measured. The judge is GPT-4o; Adv has 50 prompts; no uncertainty is reported. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and its effect on refusal.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.

The study tests affirmative prefixes, post-contexts, and decoding-order variation in LDMs. It does not test conventional adversarial suffix attacks, temperature or other decoding changes, or autoregressive chat models.
Localization of safety in weights, parameters, or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives produce shallow safety.
Training that deepens safety and its robustness.

relation.reason: Measures harmful response rates under inserted contexts and decoding-order variations, directly bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: Tests context-based refusal bypass in the new setting of diffusion language models with editable post-context and multiple decoding orders.

source_check.notes: Empty-context HR of at most 2% refers to averages over models; individual model/order cells reach 4%. TrustLDM-Auto reports 98–100% safety attack rates on the four open models; Mercury Edit 2 reaches 94% on Adv and 83% on JBB.

statements.correction: Table 1, prefix plus long suffix, Adv/JBB: LLaDA 87%/88%; LLaDA 1.5 83%/86%; Dream 81%/80%. Corresponding Empty baselines: 3%/1%, 2%/3%, 0%/0%. LLaDA 1.5 prefix plus short suffix on Adv: 93%.
statements.problem: The 80–93% range mixes short and long suffix conditions. The long-suffix conditions for the three named models span 80–88%; 93% belongs to LLaDA 1.5 with a short suffix.
